auth: Requires a Bearer token. Every endpoint here is documented against the solo owner (role `owner`, acting in a Staff-style capacity — see business-owner.md's S1/S2 stories) since that's the only fulfillment session built so far; Phase 5's Front Desk/Staff roles will extend this same domain, not replace it.

endpoints.description: Fetches bookings for a business. Supports optional `date` (single day, for Today), `from`/`to` (range, for Calendar's month view and Earnings), and `status` query params. Today/Calendar/Earnings currently all read from one client-side array that only ever holds bookings created during the current app session — a real backend needs this endpoint to actually list bookings that already existed, not just ones the app itself just created.

endpoints.screen: New appointment — Now (business-owner app, Today tab "+")
endpoints.description: Records a walk-in: the customer is already physically present, so this skips pending_payment/confirmed entirely and starts life as in_progress — no deposit, no date/time picking (server should stamp the current date/time, not trust a client-sent one). customerName falls back to "Walk-in customer" client-side if left blank; customerPhone/customerEmail are optional. staffId is optional too — null/omitted means unassigned ("Any available"/"Walk-in"); when present it's a team.json add-team-member invitationId, which is how a member's earnings view (see get-earnings-summary) knows which bookings are theirs.

errors.message: services must include at least one item

endpoints.screen: New appointment — Schedule (business-owner app, Calendar tab "+", or a customer's "New appointment" button)
endpoints.description: Owner manually books a future appointment on someone's behalf. Same shape as create-walk-in-booking (including the optional staffId assignment) plus date/time, and starts life as confirmed rather than in_progress — the owner still has to check the customer in (see update-booking-status) when they actually arrive. Uses source `walk_in` (owner-recorded) rather than a separate value, since the only real difference from a walk-in is the starting status.

endpoints.description: Drives Appointment Detail's status stepper: check-in (confirmed → in_progress), no-show, and cancel. (in_progress → completed happens via charge-booking below, not this endpoint, since completing always goes through a payment record.)

errors.message: Cannot move from completed to in_progress

endpoints.description: Records the final service charge once a booking is in_progress, and marks it completed. `method` is `mpesa` (sends an STK push to `customerPhone` through the business's connected payment destination — request must include customerPhone) or `cash` (no phone needed, records instantly). Separate from confirm-booking-payment, which is the customer-facing up-front deposit push at booking time, not this after-the-fact full charge.

errors.message: customerPhone is required when method is mpesa

endpoints.description: Revenue trend buckets, payment-method breakdown, per-service breakdown, and appointment counts for a date range (`from`/`to` query params, both 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Also takes an optional `staffId` query param — when present, scopes every number to bookings assigned to that team member (see create-walk-in-booking's staffId), which is what TeamMemberDetailScreen's earnings section needs; omitted, it's the whole-business view EarningsScreen shows. Mirrors what src/utils/earnings.ts currently computes client-side by filtering every booking in memory — fine for mock data, not something a real backend should do at scale. `services` should include every service the business currently offers, not just ones with revenue (bookingsCount: 0 rows included) — both screens use that to show what isn't selling, not just what is. Only bookings with paymentStatus 'paid' count toward any amount here.

endpoints.description: Creates or updates a customer record entered through the walk-in/schedule flow. `customerId` present means the client already matched this to an existing customer (by phone — the closest thing to a stable identifier the app has) and this is an update to their name/email; absent means create a new one.
